name: Latvia
summary: Capital gains taxed at 25.5% (from 2025) plus a 3% surtax on income above EUR 200k; foreign and domestic dividends that were taxed at source are PIT-exempt (but count for the 3% surtax); no inheritance, gift-to-children or wealth tax. Companies pay 20/80 CIT only on distribution.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Ordinary Latvian tax residence; no special regime for new wealthy arrivals.
regimes.eligibility: Declared place of residence in Latvia, or 183 days in any 12-month period.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares, funds, bonds, real estate and crypto are taxed at 25.5% (since 1 Jan 2025, up from 20%), plus the 3% additional rate on total annual income above EUR 200,000, so 28.5% at the margin for a large gain.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Latvian real estate: exempt if held 60 months and declared primary residence for 12 months, or held 60 months as the only property, or proceeds reinvested in a like property within 12 months. Capital losses offset capital gains (crypto separately).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Investment account (ieguldījumu konts): income is taxed only when withdrawals exceed deposits (PIT Law Section 11.9(11)(6) and the rule that follows it), so a listed portfolio can be rolled over without tax until money is taken out.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Transactions begun but not completed by 31 Dec 2024 and notified to the SRS remain at 20% in 2025-2027. Section 15(5) of the PIT Law: 25.5% on income from capital, including capital gains. Section 15.1 (in force 1 Jan 2026 wording): an additional 3% on the excess of total annual income over EUR 200,000, payable through the annual return; the base expressly includes taxable income 'including capital gains and income from capital' and the dividends and liquidation quotas exempted by Section 9(1)(2.1)-(2.2).

open_questions: Exact conditions for an account to qualify as an investment account (e.g. foreign brokers) not summarised here.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 25.5% capital income rate + 3% additional rate on income above EUR 200k = 28.5% for a large gain; no holding-period relief except the main-home/sole-property exemption. Investment account can defer tax on listed portfolios. 25.5% on capital income (§15(5)); the 3% additional rate above EUR 200,000 per person is in income_surtax.
capital_gains.professional_trader: No specific recharacterisation regime found; business income of a self-employed person is taxed at progressive rates (25.5%/33%) plus social contributions.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Securities: none. Latvian real estate: 60 months for the residence/sole-property exemption.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains taxed; foreign tax credited up to Latvian tax on that income.

income_surtax.notes: Additional rate (PIT Law §15.1, from 1 January 2026): 3% on the excess of a person's total income over EUR 200,000 a year, where total income includes capital gains and the dividends exempt under §9(1)(2.1); per taxpayer (no joint filing). Not indexed.

dividends.summary: Dividends are exempt from PIT when CIT was paid on the distributed profit in Latvia, or when CIT (or an equivalent tax) was paid abroad or PIT/WHT was withheld abroad on the dividend (PIT Law Section 9(1)(2.1)); otherwise taxed at 25.5%. Tax-haven dividends are always taxed. Even exempt dividends count toward the 3% additional rate on income above EUR 200,000 (Section 15.1(2)).
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Exemption needs evidence of foreign CIT or WHT (EU/EEA companies generally excepted from proof, but SRS may ask).
dividends.important_exceptions: Ordinary foreign portfolio dividends that suffered source WHT (e.g. 15% US treaty WHT) or come from a company that paid CIT abroad are exempt, not taxed at 25.5% with a credit: the statute settles the conflict with a broker article (TWINO) that described a credit method. An additional 3% PIT applies to the part of total annual income above EUR 200,000, and the base includes exempt dividends. From 2026 Latvian companies wholly owned by individuals may opt into a 15% CIT + 6% PIT dividend regime.

open_questions: Whether the SRS demands proof of foreign CIT/WHT for every portfolio dividend in practice.
dividends.rate_basis: 0% PIT on dividends from taxed profits/with foreign WHT, plus the 3% additional rate for a family whose income exceeds EUR 200k = 3%. Headline 28.5% = 25.5% + 3% for dividends not meeting the condition (e.g. tax havens). Dividends are PIT-exempt where Latvian CIT was paid or tax was withheld or paid abroad (§9(1)(2.1)); they count only towards the 3% additional rate, which is in the capital-gains income_surtax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Latvian companies pay 20% CIT on gross distributions (20/80); no WHT on dividends to non-resident companies except tax-haven residents (20%).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the structure regime 'sia_holding': a Latvian SIA pays no tax on dividends or gains it keeps; 20% of the grossed-up distribution (25% of the net amount) is due when it distributes, and the shareholder's dividend is PIT-exempt but counts toward the 3% additional rate above EUR 200,000 a year.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no recurring levy on financial assets.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax and no gift tax for children. Heirs pay a Land Register state fee only on inherited Latvian real estate: 0.25% for children who lived with the deceased, 0.5% for other children; no fee on movable property such as securities.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: No state fee if the inherited real estate is worth less than ten minimum monthly wages.

regimes.name: Latvian holding company (SIA)
regimes.description: The family holds the portfolio through a Latvian private limited company (SIA) owned by the parents. Latvia taxes a company's profit only when it is distributed or deemed distributed: 20% of the gross-up (net distribution divided by 0.8), i.e. 25% of the net amount. Dividends and gains the SIA earns and keeps are untaxed. A resident individual shareholder pays no personal income tax on a dividend from profit on which Latvian company income tax was paid (PIT Law Section 9(1)(2.1)(a)), but the exempt dividend still counts toward the 3% additional rate on a person's total annual income above EUR 200,000 (Section 15.1). Wealth tax (none) and inheritance tax (none) are the same as for direct holding, so they inherit from the standard regime.
regimes.eligibility: Any person can found an SIA (articles, Commercial Register entry). The shareholders must be Latvian tax residents for the personal-side treatment modelled here. Contributing an existing portfolio in kind is a disposal for the individual (tax at 25.5% on the gain under PIT Law Section 15(5), not verified for contributions to capital); the structure is cheapest funded with cash or newly bought positions.
regimes.duration_note: A company under ordinary law with no time limit; the distribution-based system has no sunset in the sources read.

structure.entity: sabiedrība ar ierobežotu atbildību (SIA, private limited company)
structure.payout_notes: Company income tax of 20% on the grossed-up distribution (net / 0.8), so 20% of the cash the company uses (EUR 80 paid out costs EUR 20 of tax on a EUR 100 outlay; PwC). The shareholder's dividend is exempt from personal income tax (PIT Law Section 9(1)(2.1)(a)), but counts toward the additional 3% rate on a taxpayer's total annual income above EUR 200,000 (Section 15.1(1),(2)): 3% x 80 = 2.4 per 100 of outlay at the top marginal rate, so payout_tax_rate = 0.20 + 0.024 = 0.224. A couple sharing a EUR 400,000 net payout equally sits at the EUR 200,000 threshold per person; the threshold is not indexed, and the top marginal case is assumed. Liquidation quota is exempt from PIT where Latvian company tax was paid (Section 9(1)(2.2)). Since 1 January 2026 an SIA owned only by individuals may opt for an alternative: 15% company tax on net/0.85 plus 6% PIT withheld on the dividend (PIT Law Section 15(5.1); Corporate Income Tax Law Article 4.2). Not modelled: per EUR 100 received it costs about 28.3 against 28.0 for the standard route if the 3% rate also applies, so it is not better.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: Deemed distributions are taxed at the 20/80 rate when they arise: non-business expenses, loans to related parties (with exclusions), excess interest, transfer-pricing adjustments, hybrid mismatches, assets transferred abroad (PwC). Private use of company assets or loans to the shareholders therefore costs 25% of the net amount. Dividends to tax-haven recipients are always taxed. No substance test is needed for a resident SIA holding a portfolio.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: On liquidation, surplus assets are a deemed distribution taxed at 20/80 (PwC); the liquidation quota is then PIT-exempt for the shareholder (Section 9(1)(2.2)). Exit tax on an individual who emigrates with SIA shares was not researched.

capital_gains.summary: Gains the SIA realises on shares and other assets are not taxed when realised: Latvian company income tax falls only on distributed or deemed-distributed profit. Selling and reinvesting inside the company costs nothing until money is paid out.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No holding period or minimum stake for retained gains.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Payout at 20/80 is in the structure terms, not in these rates.

capital_gains.rate_basis: 0%: PwC: 'all undistributed corporate profits are exempt', covering active and passive income and most capital gains; tax is postponed until distribution. The 20/80 charge on paying out is the structure's payout rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Not relevant: a company's trading profit is likewise untaxed until distributed.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide gains of the company are exempt until distribution.

dividends.summary: Dividends the SIA receives, from Latvian or foreign companies, are not taxed while the profit stays in the company; tax arises only when the SIA distributes. Foreign withholding on the portfolio's dividends (15% for most) is a final cost inside the SIA.
